evals.prompt: Show me how a browser form submission travels through a React page, an API endpoint, a queue, and a background worker. The API returns 202 before the worker finishes. Keep it concise and make the asynchronous boundary unmistakable.
evals.expected_output: A compact inline visual and brief interpretation that clearly separates HTTP acceptance from asynchronous processing.
expectations: The response chooses one small visual rather than combining every supported format.
The HTTP 202 response occurs before queued background work completes.
The visual has directional, specifically labelled interactions and a short text interpretation.
No file is created or application opened because the prompt asks for an inline explanation.

evals.prompt: Show me the proposed refactor from one src/transport.ts file into client, retry, and streaming modules. Nothing has been implemented yet.
evals.expected_output: A concise proposed file-tree diff that does not imply the refactor already exists.
expectations: The output uses a file tree or diff instead of an unnecessarily complex diagram.
The structure is explicitly labelled Proposed rather than Observed.
The output remains inline and does not write an artifact.

evals.prompt: Create a standalone HTML infographic at artifacts/cache-flow.html explaining our cache hit and miss flow, but do not use the network and do not overwrite anything already there.
evals.expected_output: A safe, self-contained HTML artifact in an approved location with an unused Windows-safe filename.
expectations: The artifact is self-contained and contains no remote scripts, styles, fonts, images, or telemetry.
The output path and filename are valid on Windows and an existing file is not overwritten.
User-derived text is treated as data rather than executable markup.
The response reports the artifact path without assuming the macOS open command.
